commands.author: xydt-tanshanshan

target.title: fix(doctor): preserve allowlist entries for version-bound runtime plugins during stale config scan
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a previously bundled `@openclaw/codex` plugin is externalized to an npm package, `doctor --fix` silently removes `"codex"` from `plugins.allow` during the first run after upgrade. The allowlist entry is pruned because `plugins.allow` entries are compared against `knownIds` (discovered plugin manifests) — since `@openclaw/codex` hasn't been installed yet at scan time, `"codex"` is flagged as stale and deleted.

Reported as issue #107226.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stateful repair sequencing at `src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing.ts:160` already passes `failedPluginIds` to `maybeRepairStalePluginConfig` as `preservePluginIds`, so plugins whose auto-install failed survive the stale prune. However, codex in `plugins.allow` is not tracked as a "configured plugin" entry — it's only referenced on the allowlist, not in `plugins.entries`. The auto-install step (`repairMissingConfiguredPluginInstalls`) only processes plugins referenced from `plugins.entries` or agent harness configurations, so `plugins.allow`-only entries are never in `failedPluginIds`.

The fix adds `VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS` (currently `new Set(["codex"])`) to the `preservePluginIds` spread at the call site. This is a single-owner, scalar change in the repair sequencing module — no new logic in the stale-plugin scanner, no LOC growth in the file that already exceeds the ratchet limit.

## User Impact

Transparent — `plugins.allow` entries for version-bound externalized plugins survive `doctor --fix`. No configuration change needed.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | Before | After | Changed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.allow: ["codex"]` on first post-upgrade `doctor --fix` | `"codex"` removed (silent allowlist drop) | `"codex"` preserved (survives until release backfill install) | ✅ Fix |
| `plugins.allow: ["codex"]` after `@openclaw/codex` is installed | `"codex"` kept (knownIds match) | `"codex"` kept (knownIds match) | ❌ No |
| Non-version-bound stale plugin entry (e.g., retired channel) | Removed | Removed | ❌ No |

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.18.0, branch `fix/preserve-allowlist-version-bound-107226`.

**Test results** (2026-07-14):

| Test suite | Tests | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `stale-plugin-config.test.ts` | 18 | ✅ 18 passed |
| `repair-sequencing.test.ts` | 16 | ✅ 16 passed |
| `doctor-config-flow.test.ts` | 41 | ✅ 40 passed, 1 unrelated (Node SQLite env) |

**Relevant code paths**:

`src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing.ts:160`:
```ts
preservePluginIds: [...failedPluginIds, ...VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS],
```

`VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS` is exported from `missing-configured-plugin-install.ts` as `new Set(["codex"])`.

**Scanner vs repair layering** (verified by tests):

- `scanStalePluginConfig` directly flags codex in `plugins.allow` as stale (codex is not in `knownIds`). No scanner-level exemption.
- `maybeRepairStalePluginConfig` without `preservePluginIds` removes codex from allowlist.
- `maybeRepairStalePluginConfig` called from `runDoctorRepairSequence` with `preservePluginIds: ["codex"]` preserves codex.
- The `repair-sequencing.test.ts` tests verify `preservePluginIds` propagation: `["brave", "codex"]` and `["whatsapp", "codex"]`.

**What was not tested**: Full `v2026.6.11 → v2026.7.1` end-to-end upgrade with a real gateway restart and Codex agent turn. The repair-sequencing integration tests cover the `preservePluginIds` propagation path through the entire `runDoctorRepairSequence` function, verifying that `maybeRepairStalePluginConfig` receives the combined `preservePluginIds` set.
